Differential abundance of taxa.

Source: R/taxa_da.r
taxa_da.Rd

Finds the taxa whose abundance differs between groups (stat.by) or changes with a numeric variable (regr). Unlike taxa_stats(), which tests each taxon's abundance on its own, these methods account for the compositional nature of sequencing data: a sample's counts are a sample from the community, so an increase in one taxon lowers the observed proportions of all the others. The method is LinDA (Zhou et al. 2022), built into rbiom.

Usage

taxa_da(
  biom,
  stat.by = NULL,
  regr = NULL,
  rank = -1,
  taxa = NULL,
  method = "linda",
  covariates = NULL,
  split.by = NULL,
  strata = NULL,
  prev.cut = 0.1,
  level = 0.95,
  p.adj = "fdr",
  lineage = FALSE,
  unc = "singly"
)

Arguments

biom

An rbiom object, or any value accepted by as_rbiom().

stat.by

Dataset field with the groups to compare. Must be categorical. Each pair of groups is compared, in the order of the field's levels: with levels A, B, and C, the comparisons are "B - A", "C - A", and "C - B", and a positive log fold change means the taxon is more abundant in the first-named group. Give either stat.by or regr, not both. Default: NULL

regr

Dataset field with a numeric variable. The log fold change is then per unit increase in regr. Give either stat.by or regr, not both. Default: NULL

rank

What rank(s) of taxa to test. E.g. "Phylum", "Genus", ".otu", etc. An integer vector can also be given, where 1 is the highest rank, -1 is the lowest rank, and 0 is the OTU "rank". Each rank is analyzed separately. Default: -1

taxa

Which taxa to report. An integer value reports the top n most abundant taxa, a value 0 <= n < 1 reports the taxa with that mean relative abundance or greater, and a character vector reports the named taxa. Every taxon that passes prev.cut is still part of the analysis, since LinDA estimates the compositional bias from all of them, and p-values are adjusted for all of them. Default: NULL (all tested taxa).

method

The differential abundance method. Currently only "linda". See Details. Default: "linda"

covariates

Dataset field(s) to adjust for, such as age or antibiotic use. They are included in every model, but their own effects are not reported. Default: NULL

split.by

Dataset field(s) that the samples should be split by. Each subset is analyzed separately. Must be categorical. Default: NULL

strata

Dataset field with a blocking variable, such as a subject identifier for repeated measures. Must be categorical. Adds a random intercept per stratum to every model, fitted as linear mixed models with lmerTest::lmer() (requires the lmerTest package). Default: NULL

prev.cut

Prevalence filter: taxa found in fewer than this proportion of the samples are not tested. Default: 0.1

level

The confidence level for the confidence intervals (.lower and .upper). Default: 0.95

p.adj

Method to use for multiple comparisons adjustment of p-values. Run p.adjust.methods for a list of available options. As is standard for differential abundance, p-values are adjusted across taxa separately for each comparison (and each rank and split.by subset). Default: "fdr"

lineage

Include all ranks in the name of the taxa. For instance, setting to TRUE will produce Bacteria; Actinobacteria; Coriobacteriia; Coriobacteriales. Otherwise the taxa name will simply be Coriobacteriales. You want to set this to TRUE when unc = "asis" and you have taxa names (such as Incertae_Sedis) that map to multiple higher level ranks. Default: FALSE

unc

How to handle unclassified, uncultured, and similarly ambiguous taxa names. Options are:

"singly" -

Replaces them with the OTU name.

"grouped" -

Replaces them with a higher rank's name.

"drop" -

Excludes them from the result.

"asis" -

To not check/modify any taxa names.

Abbreviations are allowed. Default: "singly"

Value

A tibble data.frame with one row per taxon and comparison, and the columns:

.rank -

The rank. Only present when several ranks were requested.

split.by fields -

The subset of samples.

stat.by field -

The comparison, e.g. "Stool - Saliva" (positive fold changes: more abundant in Stool). Absent when regr is given.

.taxa -

The taxon.

.lfc -

The bias-corrected log2 fold change: the difference in log2 abundance between the two groups, or the change per unit of regr.

.se -

The standard error of .lfc.

.lower, .upper -

The confidence interval of .lfc at level.

.t.ratio -

The test statistic, .lfc / .se.

.df -

Degrees of freedom of the t-test.

.p.val -

The p-value.

.adj.p -

.p.val adjusted for multiple comparisons across taxa (see p.adj).

.n -

The number of samples analyzed.

Rows are sorted by .p.val. The R code that reproduces the table is in $code.

Details

LinDA expects unrarefied counts: it models differences in sequencing depth itself, and rarefying discards data.

Counts. The counts are summed to rank with taxa_matrix() (using unc and lineage) and every sample with a value for all of the fields used is included. Samples with an NA in stat.by, regr, covariates, split.by, or strata are dropped (with a message).

LinDA (Zhou et al. 2022) fits one linear model per taxon to the centered log2-ratios of the counts. Compositionality shifts every taxon's coefficient by the same unknown amount; assuming that most taxa don't change, that shift is the mode of the coefficients across taxa, and subtracting it gives the log2 fold changes. rbiom's implementation follows the published algorithm and the defaults of MicrobiomeStat::linda():

  1. Taxa present in fewer than prev.cut of the samples are removed, and then any samples without counts.

  2. Each taxon's relative abundances are winsorized at its 97th percentile, and converted back to (rounded) counts.

  3. Zeros: when the sequencing depth (log of the sample sums) is associated with the model's variables (any p <= 0.1), each zero is imputed as the sample's depth divided by the largest depth among the samples where the taxon is absent. Otherwise a pseudo-count of 0.5 is added to every count.

  4. Centered log2-ratio transformation (each sample's log2 counts minus their mean).

  5. A linear model per taxon, clr ~ stat.by + covariates (or regr), fitted with stats::lm(), or with lmerTest::lmer() and a random intercept per stratum when strata is given. Numeric variables are standardized for fitting; regr's fold changes are reported per unit.

  6. Each comparison is a coefficient (regr, or a group versus the first group) or a difference of two coefficients (two other groups). Its bias is its mode across taxa, estimated by the mean-shift algorithm with a Gaussian kernel (the same estimator as modeest::mlv(method = "meanshift")), and is subtracted.

  7. The standard error comes from the coefficients' covariance, and the p-value from a t-test with the model's residual degrees of freedom (Satterthwaite's for mixed models).

For a numeric regr and for comparisons with the first group, this gives the results of MicrobiomeStat::linda(). For a comparison between two other groups, MicrobiomeStat::linda.wald.test() would subtract the difference of the two coefficients' modes; rbiom takes the mode of the difference instead, which assumes that most taxa don't differ between those two groups (rather than between each of them and the first group), and doesn't depend on which group comes first.

One deliberate difference from MicrobiomeStat::linda() (version 1.4): when it reports that sequencing depth is associated with the model, it still adds the pseudo-count, because it compares "Imputation" with "imputation"; rbiom imputes, as the paper describes.

References

Zhou H, He K, Chen J, Zhang X (2022). LinDA: linear models for differential abundance analysis of microbiome compositional data. Genome Biology 23:95. doi:10.1186/s13059-022-02655-5

See also

taxa_forest() to plot the results.

Other taxa_abundance: sample_sums(), taxa_boxplot(), taxa_clusters(), taxa_corrplot(), taxa_forest(), taxa_heatmap(), taxa_stacked(), taxa_stats(), taxa_sums(), taxa_table()

Other stats_tables: adiv_stats(), bdiv_stats(), distmat_stats(), stats_table(), taxa_stats()

Examples

    library(rbiom)

    biom <- subset(hmp50, `Body Site` %in% c("Saliva", "Stool"))

    da <- taxa_da(biom, stat.by = "Body Site", rank = "Genus")
    da
#> # Method:   LinDA (Zhou et al. 2022)
#> # Model:    log abundance ~ `Body Site`, per taxon
#> # p.adj:    FDR (Benjamini-Hochberg), across taxa within each comparison
#> # A tibble: 147 × 11
#>    `Body Site`  .taxa  .lfc   .se .lower .upper .t.ratio   .df   .p.val   .adj.p
#>    <fct>        <chr> <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl>    <dbl> <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>
#>  1 Stool - Sal… Veil… -9.40 0.393 -10.2   -8.57    -23.9    18 4.35e-15 6.40e-13
#>  2 Stool - Sal… Orib… -7.83 0.342  -8.55  -7.11    -22.9    18 9.41e-15 6.92e-13
#>  3 Stool - Sal… Prev… -7.69 0.394  -8.52  -6.86    -19.5    18 1.44e-13 7.05e-12
#>  4 Stool - Sal… Capn… -6.82 0.356  -7.57  -6.07    -19.1    18 2.06e-13 7.56e-12
#>  5 Stool - Sal… Gran… -6.46 0.347  -7.19  -5.73    -18.6    18 3.38e-13 9.92e-12
